Subject: MAP: sequencing, batching & cache assumptions — unit-econ scrub

Hi Anya / HelixMed procurement team,

Following our demo last week, we want to lock the MAP details that materially affect unit economics (tokens/$) so finance and procurement can validate ROI ahead of the POC sign-off. Quick ask: can you confirm the traffic and interaction profile below so we can finalize the cost model?

- Primary flows: clinical-note summarization (single-doc -> 1–3 prompt turns), patient intake triage (multi-turn chat, median 4 turns), CPT-coding assist (short prompts, standard length).
- Expected concurrency: peak 220 concurrent sessions, steady 60 sessions.
- Median tokens per turn (user prompt + model reply): 340 tokens (triage), 1,200 tokens (summarization), 95 tokens (coding).
- Desired P50 latency: <350ms; acceptable tail to 800ms for batch windows.

Key MAP items we need to validate on your side:
1) Token accounting policy — do you want us to include system prompt + metadata in per-turn tokens, or should we scope to user-visible tokens?
2) Caching tolerance — is reuse of previous patient context allowed across requests (prefix caching) or must the model see full canonical context each time?
3) Batch/latency tradeoff — are you okay with small batching windows (20–50ms) to improve tokens/$ if P95 stays below 800ms?

Attached: helix_token_estimates.csv (your initial traffic numbers plugged into our estimator).

Proposed MAP timeline (draft):
- 10/08: finalize token accounting + caching policy (you)
- 10/12: Redwood delivers updated unit-econ model (tokens/$) + baseline latency matrix
- 10/18: joint sign-off on MAP and procurement SOW
- 10/26: pilot contract executed / POC kickoff

If you can confirm the token accounting preference and whether prefix/session caching is acceptable, we’ll run a quick sensitivity sweep (quantization + batching) and push the updated numbers by 10/12.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate internally if we need infra or security docs for procurement.

Best,

Thanks Nikhil — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Token policy: procurement prefers that the vendor (Redwood) models total billable tokens including system prompts; procurement will discount any tokens attributable to patient PHI that we redact server-side, but we need visibility into token composition.
- Caching: we can accept prefix/session caching for the triage flow (user consented session data), but not for historical medical records — those must be sent in full every time.
- Latency: 800ms P95 is a hard ceiling for patient-facing triage; summarization can tolerate 1.2s at P95 in batch windows.

We’ll take a look at your CSV and come back with any corrections; procurement wants the MAP milestones tightened where possible. Also, can you confirm whether a small prefetch (server-initiated context warm) is feasible to reduce cold-start token cost?

Regards,

Hi all — quick technical note from infra/serving side to help procurement and engineering weigh tradeoffs.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Batching: for mixed workload (triage + summarization + coding) we recommend adaptive batching with an elastic target batch size 8–16 for GPU-backed instances; this balances per-token throughput gains and latency SLOs.
- Sequence length distribution: assume a bimodal distribution (short ~120 tokens, long ~1,300 tokens). Cost model must reflect token amplification on long sequences due to KV cache churn; plan 10–12% extra tokens for cache overhead in summarization.
- Caching: implement prefix caching for consented triage sessions. For historical records, require an integrity check on payload (hash) and avoid shared prefix reuse. We can support per-session KV cache with TTL=30s to capture quick follow-ups and reduce repeated prefix re-encoding.
- Prefetching: server-initiated prefetch (warming KV texture for known next-turn prompts) reduces cold-start latency but increases token consumption marginally (prefetch payload ~0.6x of subsequent user turn). Recommend making prefetch optional and visible in billing breakdown.

Attached: batching-modeling-notes.pdf — contains quick graphs and cost sensitivity table (batch size vs tokens/$ vs P95).

Action items I’ll own:
1) Run a sensitivity sweep: batch sizes [4,8,16], cache TTL [15s,30s,60s], quantization profiles (int8 vs fp16) and produce a tokens/$ delta for HelixMed sample traffic by 10/12.
2) Produce a redline for MAP describing exactly which flows will use prefix caching vs stateless payload delivery.

If procurement is OK with explicit billing flags (prefetch=true, cache_used=true), finance can reconcile disputed token lines more easily. Happy to take this into a short call.

—Karthik

Thanks Anya — appreciate the quick response and the procurement guardrails. Summary and agreed next steps:

Agreed points:
- Token accounting: Redwood will produce a line-item tokens export that includes system prompts, model metadata, and flags for prefetched/cached content so HelixMed can see token composition.
- Caching: prefix/session caching is acceptable for triage (consented sessions). Historical medical record flows will be stateless (no prefix reuse). We will include an explicit MAP clause describing allowed cache types.
- Latency windows: triage P95 <= 800ms; summarization P95 <= 1.2s in batch windows.

Deliverables and dates:
- 10/12: Redwood delivers sensitivity sweep (batch sizes, cache TTL, quant profiles) + updated tokens/$ table — attachment: batching-modeling-notes.pdf
